## Purpose and Entry Points
This Go repository implements the GitHub MCP Server: an MCP-facing adapter that lets AI hosts invoke GitHub repository, issue, PR, workflow, security, and collaboration operations. The primary binary is `cmd/github-mcp-server/main.go`, supporting local stdio and HTTP serving; `cmd/mcpcurl/main.go` is a separate MCP client/diagnostic CLI. Container distribution is defined by `Dockerfile`.

## Server Composition
Startup parses configuration, establishes authentication/API clients, builds the MCP server, and selects its transport. `internal/ghmcp/server.go` coordinates application-level server construction, while `pkg/github/server.go` registers GitHub capabilities and `pkg/http/server.go` exposes streamable HTTP behavior. MCP protocol integration is based on the Go SDK vendored under `third-party/github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`.

## Tool Registration and Capability Policy
GitHub functionality is organized into toolsets and individual tools. `pkg/github/tools.go` and `pkg/github/inventory.go` define/register the available GitHub tools; `pkg/inventory/registry.go` and `pkg/inventory/builder.go` model the selectable tool/resource/prompt inventory. Toolset/tool allow-lists, read-only exclusion of mutation tools, feature flags, and compatibility aliases form a startup-time capability boundary in `pkg/github/scope_filter.go`, `pkg/github/feature_flags.go`, and `pkg/github/deprecated_tool_aliases.go`.

## Request Execution Flow
An MCP request is decoded by the selected transport, resolved to a registered tool, then executes against GitHub through shared request context and API clients. GitHub domain implementations are grouped by capability—for example `pkg/github/repositories.go`, `pkg/github/issues.go`, and `pkg/github/pullrequests.go`—rather than a separate service layer per API. Shared request state, tokens, GraphQL feature flags, and MCP metadata flow through `pkg/context/request.go`, `pkg/context/token.go`, and `pkg/context/graphql_features.go`.

## Authentication and GitHub Boundary
The server supports PATs, OAuth, and GitHub App authentication against GitHub.com, GHES, and ghe.com. OAuth lifecycle and browser/device callback handling reside in `internal/oauth/flow.go`, `internal/oauth/manager.go`, and `internal/oauth/callback.go`; GitHub App credentials are handled by `internal/githubapp/githubapp.go`. GitHub REST and GraphQL calls are an external-service boundary, with HTTP client concerns such as bearer auth, ETags, user agent, and GraphQL headers in `pkg/http/transport/bearer.go`, `pkg/http/transport/etag.go`, and `pkg/http/transport/graphql_features.go`.

## HTTP Security and Per-Request Controls
HTTP mode layers parsing and security middleware before MCP dispatch. `pkg/http/handler.go` is the request handler boundary; middleware handles body limits, CORS, MCP parsing, token extraction, request configuration, scope challenges, and PAT scope checks under `pkg/http/middleware/`. Operator configuration is an upper bound, while selected request headers can enable certain per-request restrictions.

## Content Safety, Output, and UI Resources
Lockdown filtering is a best-effort content-safety layer over returned public-repository content, not an authorization system; its logic is in `pkg/lockdown/lockdown.go` and GitHub integration in `pkg/github/lockdown.go`. Output shaping/sanitization and error translation are centralized in `pkg/sanitize/sanitize.go` and `pkg/errors/error.go`. Some MCP tools expose embedded interactive UI resources: Go embedding/registration is in `pkg/github/ui_embed.go` and `pkg/github/ui_tools.go`, backed by TypeScript/React applications in `ui/src/apps/`.

## Runtime and Delivery
The principal runtime is a Go executable, used directly or as the public `ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server` Docker image. The UI is a separately built Node/Vite artifact incorporated into Go’s UI distribution path (`ui/scripts/build.mjs`, `pkg/github/ui_dist/`). Releases and container publication are automated through `.github/workflows/goreleaser.yml` and `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`.
